post.caption:
Inflation comes from money supply, demand and rising costs all pushing the same way. Central banks target a low steady rate rather than zero, because deflation is worse: if prices fall, everyone waits to buy, which means less selling and fewer jobs. The practical consequence is the useful one. Cash sitting idle loses purchasing power every year, by design. Holding it is a decision, not a neutral default.
